```{r setup}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(rtables)
library(emmeans)
library(ggplot2)

adqsadas_path <- "data/adam/adqsadas.xpt"
t4_csv_path   <- "outputs/t4_adascog_wk24_ancova.csv"

trt_levels <- c("Placebo", "Xanomeline Low Dose", "Xanomeline High Dose")
# Okabe-Ito, as in programs/92_figures.R
trt_colours <- c("Placebo" = "#0072B2", "Xanomeline Low Dose" = "#E69F00",
                 "Xanomeline High Dose" = "#D55E00")

# Formatting helpers, identical to programs/93_tables_tte_eff.R
fmt_p <- function(p) if (is.na(p)) "NA" else if (p < 0.001) "<0.001" else sprintf("%.3f", p)
fmt_ci <- function(est, lo, hi, d = 1) {
  f <- function(x) if (is.na(x)) "NE" else formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
  paste0(f(est), " (", f(lo), ", ", f(hi), ")")
}

# SAS transport stores missing character values as "".
adqsadas <- read_xpt(adqsadas_path) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(.x, "")))
```

# Purpose

This report covers the primary efficacy analysis of the CDISC pilot study
CDISCPILOT01. The endpoint is the change from baseline in the ADAS-Cog(11) total
score at Week 24, with missing Week 24 values imputed by last observation
carried forward (LOCF). The analysis is an ANCOVA in the efficacy population.

The report reads the submission-ready transport file `r adqsadas_path` and
rebuilds Table 4 from it. It then:

- checks that Table 4 is identical to the table produced by
  `programs/93_tables_tte_eff.R`;
- shows the model in full and checks its assumptions;
- adds exploratory sensitivity analyses to the LOCF result.

Analysis conventions (populations, windows, LOCF) are in
[`docs/sap.md`](../docs/sap.md). The dataset context is in
[`docs/adrg.md`](../docs/adrg.md).

# Analysis set

The analysis records are the ADAS-Cog total score (`PARAMCD = "ACTOT"`)
records that meet all of the following:

- in the efficacy population (`EFFFL = "Y"`);
- in the Week 24 window (`AVISITN = 24`);
- flagged as analysed (`ANL01FL = "Y"`).

Treatment is planned treatment (`TRTP`). These are the same records as in
`programs/93_tables_tte_eff.R`.

```{r analysis-set}
wk24 <- adqsadas %>%
  filter(PARAMCD == "ACTOT", EFFFL == "Y", AVISITN == 24, ANL01FL == "Y") %>%
  mutate(TRTP = factor(TRTP, levels = trt_levels))

stopifnot(
  nrow(wk24) == n_distinct(wk24$USUBJID),  # one analysed Week 24 record per subject
  !anyNA(wk24$CHG),
  !anyNA(wk24$BASE),
  !anyNA(wk24$SITEGR1)
)

effpop <- adqsadas %>%
  filter(PARAMCD == "ACTOT", EFFFL == "Y") %>%
  distinct(USUBJID, TRTP) %>%
  count(TRTP = factor(TRTP, levels = trt_levels), name = "Efficacy population")

wk24 %>%
  group_by(TRTP) %>%
  summarise(
    `Analysed at Week 24` = n(),
    `Observed at Week 24` = sum(is.na(DTYPE)),
    `Imputed by LOCF`     = sum(DTYPE %in% "LOCF"),
    `Week 24 completers (COMP24FL)` = sum(COMP24FL %in% "Y"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(effpop, by = "TRTP") %>%
  relocate(`Efficacy population`, .after = TRTP) %>%
  rename(Treatment = TRTP)
```

The proportion of LOCF-imputed values is much higher in the two xanomeline arms
than in placebo. That difference comes from more early discontinuations in the
active arms. It is the main reason for the sensitivity analyses in
@sec-sensitivity.

# Descriptive summary

```{r by-visit}
by_visit <- adqsadas %>%
  filter(PARAMCD == "ACTOT", EFFFL == "Y", ANL01FL == "Y") %>%
  mutate(TRTP = factor(TRTP, levels = trt_levels),
         AVISIT = reorder(factor(AVISIT), AVISITN)) %>%
  group_by(TRTP, AVISITN, AVISIT) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(AVAL), sd = sd(AVAL), se = sd / sqrt(n),
            n_locf = sum(DTYPE %in% "LOCF"), .groups = "drop")

by_visit %>%
  transmute(Treatment = TRTP, Visit = AVISIT, n,
            `Mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", mean, sd),
            `of which LOCF` = n_locf)
```

```{r fig-by-visit}
#| fig-cap: "ADAS-Cog(11) total score by analysis visit, mean ± 1 SE (efficacy population, LOCF). Higher scores indicate worse cognition."
ggplot(by_visit, aes(AVISITN, mean, colour = TRTP, shape = TRTP)) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 1.5)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, position = position_dodge(width = 1.5)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), width = 1.5,
                position = position_dodge(width = 1.5)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 8, 16, 24),
                     labels = c("Baseline", "Week 8", "Week 16", "Week 24")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = trt_colours) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "ADAS-Cog(11) total score", colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

```{r fig-chg-dist}
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of change from baseline to Week 24 (LOCF) by treatment. Diamonds mark the arm mean."
ggplot(wk24, aes(TRTP, CHG, fill = TRTP)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.35, outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = TRTP), width = 0.12, height = 0, alpha = 0.6, size = 1.4) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 23, size = 3.5, fill = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = trt_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = trt_colours, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Change from baseline at Week 24") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

# Primary analysis: Table 4

The model is an ANCOVA:

$$
\text{CHG}_i = \mu + \tau_{\text{TRTP}(i)} + \gamma_{\text{SITEGR1}(i)} + \beta \cdot \text{BASE}_i + \varepsilon_i,
\qquad \varepsilon_i \sim N(0, \sigma^2)
$$

- **Least-squares means.** Computed with {emmeans}, averaging over pooled site
  with equal weights.
- **Comparisons with placebo.** Not adjusted for multiplicity.
- **Dose-response test.** The same model with dose (0, 54, 81 mg, `TRTPN`) as a
  continuous term in place of the treatment factor.

```{r ancova}
by_arm <- wk24 %>%
  group_by(TRTP, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  summarise(
    n      = n(),
    base   = sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", mean(BASE), sd(BASE)),
    wk     = sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", mean(AVAL), sd(AVAL)),
    chg    = sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", mean(CHG), sd(CHG)),
    n_locf = sum(DTYPE %in% "LOCF"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

fit   <- lm(CHG ~ TRTP + SITEGR1 + BASE, data = wk24)
emm   <- emmeans(fit, ~ TRTP)
lsm   <- summary(emm)
diffs <- summary(contrast(emm, method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1, adjust = "none"),
                 infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

dose_fit <- lm(CHG ~ TRTPN + SITEGR1 + BASE, data = wk24)
p_dose   <- summary(dose_fit)$coefficients["TRTPN", "Pr(>|t|)"]

t4 <- rtable(
  header = rheader(rrow("", trt_levels[1], trt_levels[2], trt_levels[3]),
                   rrow("", paste0("(N=", by_arm$n[1], ")"), paste0("(N=", by_arm$n[2], ")"),
                        paste0("(N=", by_arm$n[3], ")"))),
  rrow("Baseline, mean (SD)", by_arm$base[1], by_arm$base[2], by_arm$base[3]),
  rrow("Week 24, mean (SD)", by_arm$wk[1], by_arm$wk[2], by_arm$wk[3]),
  rrow("Change from baseline, mean (SD)", by_arm$chg[1], by_arm$chg[2], by_arm$chg[3]),
  rrow("  of which Week 24 value by LOCF, n", by_arm$n_locf[1], by_arm$n_locf[2],
       by_arm$n_locf[3]),
  rrow("LS mean change (SE)",
       sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", lsm$emmean[1], lsm$SE[1]),
       sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", lsm$emmean[2], lsm$SE[2]),
       sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", lsm$emmean[3], lsm$SE[3])),
  rrow("LS mean difference vs placebo (95% CI)", "",
       fmt_ci(diffs$estimate[1], diffs$lower.CL[1], diffs$upper.CL[1]),
       fmt_ci(diffs$estimate[2], diffs$lower.CL[2], diffs$upper.CL[2])),
  rrow("p-value vs placebo", "", fmt_p(diffs$p.value[1]), fmt_p(diffs$p.value[2])),
  rrow("Dose-response p-value", fmt_p(p_dose), "", "")
)
main_title(t4) <- "Table 4. ADAS-Cog(11) Total Score: Change from Baseline to Week 24 (LOCF)"
subtitles(t4)  <- "Efficacy Population (EFFFL = 'Y'); planned treatment (TRTP)"
main_footer(t4) <- c(
  "ANCOVA: CHG = treatment + pooled site (SITEGR1) + baseline score. LS means from emmeans;",
  "differences and p-values unadjusted for multiplicity. Dose-response: same model with dose",
  "(0, 54, 81 mg) as a continuous term. Week 24 window: study day > 140; LOCF from the last",
  "analysed value (ANL01FL = 'Y'). Higher ADAS-Cog scores indicate worse cognition."
)
prov_footer(t4) <- "Source: ADQSADAS (PARAMCD = 'ACTOT') | data/adam/adqsadas.xpt"
```

## Agreement with the program output

The table above is compared cell by cell with
`r t4_csv_path`, the result data written by
`programs/93_tables_tte_eff.R`. The render stops if any cell differs. This way
the report and the program cannot drift apart.

```{r agreement}
cells <- function(df) {
  df <- as.data.frame(df)
  vals <- df[, utils::tail(names(df), 3)]
  vals[] <- lapply(vals, function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", as.character(x)))
  cbind(row = df$row_name, vals)
}
report_cells  <- cells(as_result_df(t4, data_format = "strings"))
program_cells <- cells(read_csv(t4_csv_path, col_types = cols(.default = "c"),
                                trim_ws = FALSE, na = character()))
names(report_cells) <- names(program_cells) <- c("Row", trt_levels)

same <- dim(report_cells) == dim(program_cells)
stopifnot(all(same))
match_mat <- as.matrix(report_cells) == as.matrix(program_cells)
stopifnot("Table 4 in the report differs from outputs/t4_adascog_wk24_ancova.csv" =
            all(match_mat))

tibble(
  `Cells compared` = length(match_mat),
  `Identical`      = sum(match_mat),
  `Different`      = sum(!match_mat)
)
```

The Ns, the differences from placebo, their 95% confidence intervals and the
p-values are equal to the published pilot table. The R Consortium submission
pilot reproduces that table
([tlf-primary](https://rconsortium.github.io/submissions-pilot1/articles/tlf-primary.html)).

# Model details

## Analysis of variance

```{r anova}
fmt_aov <- function(a) {
  data.frame(Term = rownames(a), Df = a$Df,
             `Sum Sq` = round(a$`Sum Sq`, 2),
             `F value` = round(a$`F value`, 3),
             `Pr(>F)` = vapply(a$`Pr(>F)`, fmt_p, ""),
             check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}
type3 <- drop1(fit, test = "F")
type3 <- data.frame(Df = type3$Df, `Sum Sq` = type3$`Sum of Sq`,
                    `F value` = type3$`F value`, `Pr(>F)` = type3$`Pr(>F)`,
                    row.names = rownames(type3), check.names = FALSE)[-1, ]
fmt_aov(type3)
```

These are Type III-style tests: each term is dropped from the full model in
turn. The overall test for treatment uses 2 degrees of freedom, so it is a
different test from the pairwise comparisons in Table 4.

## Parameter estimates

```{r coefs}
co <- summary(fit)$coefficients
ci <- confint(fit)
data.frame(
  Term       = rownames(co),
  Estimate   = round(co[, "Estimate"], 3),
  SE         = round(co[, "Std. Error"], 3),
  `95% CI`   = sprintf("(%.2f, %.2f)", ci[, 1], ci[, 2]),
  `p-value`  = vapply(co[, "Pr(>|t|)"], fmt_p, ""),
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
)
```

- Residual SD: `r sprintf("%.2f", sigma(fit))`
- Residual degrees of freedom: `r df.residual(fit)`
- R²: `r sprintf("%.3f", summary(fit)$r.squared)`

## LS means and differences

```{r fig-forest}
#| fig-cap: "LS mean difference from placebo in change from baseline to Week 24, with 95% CI. Negative values favour xanomeline."
#| fig-height: 2.6
forest <- as.data.frame(diffs) %>%
  mutate(contrast = sub(" - Placebo", "", contrast),
         contrast = factor(contrast, levels = rev(trt_levels[-1])))
ggplot(forest, aes(estimate, contrast)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linetype = 2) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower.CL, xmax = upper.CL), height = 0.15) +
  geom_point(size = 3, colour = trt_colours[as.character(forest$contrast)]) +
  labs(x = "Difference vs placebo (points)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

# Model checks

```{r fig-diagnostics}
#| fig-cap: "Residual diagnostics for the primary ANCOVA: residuals against fitted values (left) and normal Q-Q plot (right)."
#| fig-height: 3.6
diag_df <- data.frame(fitted = fitted(fit), resid = rstandard(fit), TRTP = wk24$TRTP)
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
plot(diag_df$fitted, diag_df$resid, pch = 19, cex = 0.6,
     col = adjustcolor(trt_colours[as.character(diag_df$TRTP)], 0.7),
     xlab = "Fitted value", ylab = "Standardised residual")
abline(h = 0, col = "grey50", lty = 2)
qqnorm(diag_df$resid, main = "", pch = 19, cex = 0.6, col = "grey30")
qqline(diag_df$resid, col = "grey50", lty = 2)
par(op)
```

```{r assumptions}
slopes <- anova(fit, lm(CHG ~ TRTP * BASE + SITEGR1, data = wk24))
levene <- anova(lm(abs(resid(fit) - ave(resid(fit), wk24$TRTP, FUN = median)) ~ TRTP,
                   data = wk24))
sw <- shapiro.test(resid(fit))

tibble(
  Check = c("Homogeneity of slopes (treatment x baseline)",
            "Equal residual variance across arms (Brown-Forsythe)",
            "Normality of residuals (Shapiro-Wilk)"),
  Statistic = c(sprintf("F = %.2f on %d df", slopes$F[2], slopes$Df[2]),
                sprintf("F = %.2f on %d df", levene$`F value`[1], levene$Df[1]),
                sprintf("W = %.3f", sw$statistic)),
  `p-value` = c(fmt_p(slopes$`Pr(>F)`[2]), fmt_p(levene$`Pr(>F)`[1]), fmt_p(sw$p.value))
)
```

The homogeneity-of-slopes test checks the assumption of a common baseline
slope. With `r nrow(wk24)` subjects, the ANCOVA estimates are robust to moderate
departures from normality of the residuals. The Q-Q plot is the main guide to
how large any departure is.

# Sensitivity analyses {#sec-sensitivity}

These analyses are **exploratory**. They are not part of the pre-specified
analysis in `docs/sap.md`. They test whether the conclusion depends on how
LOCF handles missing Week 24 values:

1. **Observed cases.** The primary ANCOVA on subjects with an observed (not
   imputed) Week 24 value.
2. **Week 24 completers.** The primary ANCOVA restricted to `COMP24FL = "Y"`.
3. **Mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM).** Uses all observed
   post-baseline values at Weeks 8, 16 and 24, with no imputation. The model is
   fitted with `nlme::gls`. Fixed effects: treatment × visit, pooled site and
   baseline × visit. The within-subject covariance is unstructured. The
   estimates are the Week 24 contrasts. This model assumes the missing values
   are missing at random (MAR) rather than LOCF.

```{r sensitivity}
ancova_diffs <- function(d, label) {
  f <- lm(CHG ~ TRTP + SITEGR1 + BASE, data = d)
  s <- summary(contrast(emmeans(f, ~ TRTP), method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1,
                        adjust = "none"), infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
  n <- table(d$TRTP)
  data.frame(Analysis = label,
             N = sprintf("%d / %d / %d", n[1], n[2], n[3]),
             Comparison = sub(" - Placebo", "", s$contrast),
             estimate = s$estimate, lower = s$lower.CL, upper = s$upper.CL,
             p = s$p.value)
}

obs <- adqsadas %>%
  filter(PARAMCD == "ACTOT", EFFFL == "Y", ANL01FL == "Y", AVISITN > 0,
         is.na(DTYPE)) %>%
  mutate(TRTP = factor(TRTP, levels = trt_levels),
         AVISIT = factor(AVISITN, levels = c(8, 16, 24),
                         labels = c("Week 8", "Week 16", "Week 24"))) %>%
  arrange(USUBJID, AVISITN)

mmrm <- nlme::gls(
  CHG ~ TRTP * AVISIT + SITEGR1 + BASE * AVISIT,
  data = obs,
  correlation = nlme::corSymm(form = ~ as.integer(AVISIT) | USUBJID),
  weights = nlme::varIdent(form = ~ 1 | AVISIT),
  method = "REML", na.action = na.omit
)
mmrm_s <- summary(contrast(emmeans(mmrm, ~ TRTP | AVISIT, mode = "df.error"),
                           method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1, adjust = "none"),
                  infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% filter(AVISIT == "Week 24")
n_mmrm <- table(distinct(obs, USUBJID, TRTP)$TRTP)

sens <- bind_rows(
  ancova_diffs(wk24, "Primary: ANCOVA, LOCF"),
  ancova_diffs(filter(wk24, is.na(DTYPE)), "ANCOVA, observed cases"),
  ancova_diffs(filter(wk24, COMP24FL %in% "Y"), "ANCOVA, Week 24 completers"),
  data.frame(Analysis = "MMRM, observed data (MAR)",
             N = sprintf("%d / %d / %d", n_mmrm[1], n_mmrm[2], n_mmrm[3]),
             Comparison = sub(" - Placebo", "", mmrm_s$contrast),
             estimate = mmrm_s$estimate, lower = mmrm_s$lower.CL,
             upper = mmrm_s$upper.CL, p = mmrm_s$p.value)
) %>%
  mutate(Analysis = factor(Analysis, levels = unique(Analysis)))

sens %>%
  transmute(Analysis, `N (Pbo / Low / High)` = N, Comparison,
            `Difference vs placebo (95% CI)` = mapply(fmt_ci, estimate, lower, upper),
            `p-value` = vapply(p, fmt_p, ""))
```

```{r fig-sensitivity}
#| fig-cap: "Difference from placebo at Week 24 (95% CI) under each analysis. Negative values favour xanomeline."
#| fig-height: 3.8
ggplot(sens, aes(estimate, Analysis, colour = Comparison)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linetype = 2) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), height = 0.2,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = trt_colours[-1], breaks = trt_levels[-1]) +
  labs(x = "Difference vs placebo (points)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

Under every analysis, the confidence intervals for both doses include zero.
The primary conclusion therefore does not depend on LOCF: there is no
statistically significant difference from placebo in ADAS-Cog(11) change at
Week 24. The observed-case and completer analyses keep only subjects who stayed
in the study. Those subjects are a selected group, especially in the active
arms with their higher dropout, so these two analyses complement the primary
analysis and do not replace it.
